title: Polaris Framework
subtitle: Strategic KPI governance and 90-day execution architecture — answering one question per cycle: what must be true in 90 days to de-risk the next stage, and how do we get there?

sections.heading: KPI Governance That Connects Operations to Capital Decisions
sections.body:
The Polaris Framework translates strategic intent into a measurable, board-level KPI dashboard — connecting physical operations, digital acquisition funnels, and human capacity directly to capital allocation decisions. Every metric is chosen because it drives a specific governance decision, not because it is easy to collect.

CLV:CAC >= 3:1 — The board-level profitability metric. Customer Lifetime Value must be at least 3x the cost of acquiring that customer. Below this threshold, growth destroys value.

CAC PAYBACK PERIOD — The operational cash flow instrument. Tracks how long it takes to recover acquisition cost — critical for ventures with seasonal inventory peaks or high upfront deployment costs.

OEE >= 85% — Overall Equipment Effectiveness. Primary operational maturity indicator. Below 70% is a red flag in the 6Sense Capacity dimension.

OTIF >= 98% — On-Time In-Full delivery rate. Primary trust indicator in B2C venture screening. Logistics failure = direct destruction of brand equity.

CCC < 40 DAYS (SaaS) — Cash Conversion Cycle. Measures how efficiently working capital is deployed. SaaS target: < 40 days. Physical operations: < 60 days.

OCF MARGIN > 40% — Operating Cash Flow margin. The sustainability indicator for asset-light SaaS models.

QUICK RATIO > 1.0x — Liquidity test. Below 1.0x is an automatic 6Sense Risk flag. No exceptions.

SPATIAL YIELD — Revenue per square metre. Capacity management indicator for ventures with physical distribution or retail points.

sections.heading: Hybrid Agile Execution — Not One Size Fits All
sections.body:
Polaris 90-day sprints combine high-velocity Scrum and Kanban cycles for product development with gated milestone patterns for regulatory governance. Teams iterate rapidly while maintaining full auditability — which is non-negotiable in regulated sectors.

Each sprint produces evidence, not features. The output is a validated or falsified hypothesis that changes the capital-commitment decision for the next stage.

> Track Synchronisation Protocol (TSP): physical compliance milestones and digital sprint deliverables are synchronised via explicit handover KPIs — ensuring that regulatory gate-passes and product iterations move in lockstep, not in parallel silos.

sections.heading: Capital Velocity and Bottleneck Removal
sections.body:
Applying Theory of Constraints and RACI matrices, each 90-day sprint targets the highest-bandwidth constraint in the system. Operational lead times are shortened. Cash Conversion Cycles are optimised. Path-to-market is accelerated.

Sprint design begins with one question: where is the highest-bandwidth feedback environment available to test the critical hypothesis? Validation happens there first — before capital is committed to scale.

sections.heading: Knowledge That Survives the Sprint
sections.body:
Every Polaris sprint that deploys new capability into a portfolio company includes the design of an internal champion network — a super-user layer that ensures knowledge survives the sprint team's exit.

Capability that lives only in the deploying team evaporates when the engagement ends. The champion network converts sprint outcomes into durable organisational change — and it is designed before the sprint begins, not retrofitted at the end.
